To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the technique of Yokoo et al (2002) can be extended to solve distributed constraint optimization problems (DisOCSPs), while the technique of SilagHI (2003) can be extended for solving DisCSPs and DisOCSPs with privacy guarantees.
we found a technique that allows solving DisCSPs with privacy guarantees and that it can be extended to solve distributed weighted CSPs without leaking information about the quality of the solution.

(1) we introduce a first technique allowing to solve DisCSPs without revealing anything, without trusting each other, or any server; (2) we improve the privacy, efficiency and applicability of that technique, by a factor of d/sup m/, for m variables, domain size d; (3) we improve the technique to solve distributed optimization problems, without leaking sensitive information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
privacy in distributed negotiation/cooperation, and in particular with privacy-preserving distributed optimization.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have improved both efficiency and privacy in the distributed constraint satisfaction and optimization framework.

we provide a way to solve distributed constraint satisfaction and optimization problems with privacy enforcement, while the previous techniques only provide privacy enforcement with no guarantees for the solution.
we have a technique that can solve distributed constraint optimization problems (DisOCSPs) in a privacy-preserving manner, while being efficient for small problems and inapplicable for large ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an improvement of privacy guarantees for solving DisCSPs, while maintaining the same efficiency.

, for the first time, we provide a technique for solving a class of DisCSPs and optimization problems without revealing anything and while not trusting anybody, and we provide a technique that improves significantly the privacy of the existing ones.
we have a new technique that can be used to solve DisCSPs with privacy guarantees.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the problem of privacy enforcement in distributed constraint optimization can be reduced to the problem of privacy in distributed weighted CSPs, which in turn can be reduced to that of privacy in distributed CSPs.
, for the problems we consider, privacy is a fundamental requirement and should be enforced, even if this is achieved by a technique that is less efficient than the existing ones.
privacy is an essential issue to be taken into account when designing distributed constraint satisfaction algorithms.
